# Never the Number: Structural Abstention for AI Systems Whose Answers Are Consumed as Fact

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#structural-abstention)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-09**

[Original source](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.13926v1) · arXiv:2608.13926v1, 14 August 2026

**Reading coverage:** All 26 pages: sections 1–15, algorithms, architecture/schematic figures, tables and appendices A–D with synthetic compilation example and abandoned-model procedure.

## Research question

A plausible wrong number can be consumed as fact by users who cannot inspect SQL.

## Method

The proposed generative shell interprets and elicits typed slots, while an authored template pool and deterministic compiler control executable requests. Users confirm the resolved question before execution; unsupported shapes lead to clarification or disclosure of supported alternatives.

## Evaluation

This is a conceptual architecture report and retrospective account of one deployment, plus worked hypothetical transfers to two other domains. No quantitative accuracy, latency, adoption or user-error-detection evaluation is supplied; diagrams and numeric examples are illustrative.

## What the results support

The report argues that capability boundaries become inspectable when question shapes and compilation are explicit. It describes a later tool-retrieval successor and an abandoned fine-tuned parser, but their comparative advantages are qualitative observations.

## Limits and qualifications

Correctness depends on the authored mapping, compiler and meaningful user confirmation. Section 3.4 explicitly admits mis-authored templates and careless assent, qualifying statements elsewhere that failures are only visible refusals. Outside-pool requests may be answerable in principle. The action-execution extension is proposed, not implemented or evaluated.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

An architectural distinction between expressibility-based refusal and statistical abstention, with its coverage and trust assumptions made explicit.
